VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
MEMORANDUM

To: Rob Castellano, Chief Executive Officer
Rachel Steinberg, General Counsel
Hannah Berg, FP&A Manager

From: Owen Park, Chief Financial Officer

Date: August 5, 2022

Subject: Q3 2022 Apex Litigation Reserve — Draft Memo

Attached is the current draft for the Q3 close materials. I am circulating this now because the proposed reserve is material enough that I do not want the first substantive discussion to occur in the audit committee pre-read.

We are proposing an $18.0 million reserve for ApexHip-related claims and associated costs in Q3 2022. The working allocation is as follows:

| Component | Proposed Reserve | Basis |
|---|---:|---|
| Anticipated product-liability / litigation exposure | $11.0M | Filed and threatened patient claims, counsel assessment, complaint trend, revision signal |
| Customer-service warranty and replacement costs | $7.0M | Routine replacement product, credits, customer handling and related service costs |
| Total | $18.0M |  |

The $11.0M litigation component remains an estimate rather than a case-specific accrual schedule. We have a relatively small number of asserted claims today, but the underlying indicators are moving in the wrong direction. In particular, the March 2021 NJR reporting showed a five-year Apex revision rate of 7.1%, compared with a 3.2% class average. The later registry information has not provided a basis to dismiss that signal. TrackWise complaint counts also continue to rise, including complaints involving elevated Co/Cr levels, pain, suspected ARMD, and early revision.

The $7.0M customer-service component is limited to routine support for distributed product. That estimate includes expected replacement and credit exposure, customer administrative costs where contractually required, return processing, and an allowance for additional warranty requests. It does not assume that the service requests and the metal-ion allegations share a common cause. For accounting purposes, however, both items are Apex-related and need to be visible together in the Q3 discussion.

Hannah: please run the variance cases against the current FY22 forecast and provide (1) the Q3 P&L effect, (2) cash timing through Q4 2023, and (3) the revenue sensitivity if accounts defer Apex purchases following the recall notice. I would also like a base, downside, and severe-case view rather than a single-point estimate.

Rachel: please review the proposed contingency language, especially the distinction between known recall costs and estimated exposure from asserted or anticipated claims. I do not want us to overstate certainty where the claims landscape is still developing, but the committee will reasonably ask why the reserve is increasing now.

Rob: absent a significant change in the underlying numbers, my recommendation is that we book the full $18.0M in Q3 and discuss it with the audit committee as a discrete Apex matter rather than burying it in the broader warranty line.

Please send comments by noon Monday so we can finalize the pre-read package.

Owen

Dana—summarizing briefly: Tom completed off-label wear simulator re-runs at 55° cup inclination showing elevated wear rates (4–6x baseline). He is connecting this to the cluster of metal-ion complaints we logged last August from Atlanta (specifically TrackWise records TW-2018-0311, TW-2018-0312, and TW-2018-0315 out of Dr. Feld’s group).

Per our SOPs, we need your guidance on two fronts:

2. Regulatory clearly needs a formal briefing before any ECO-2019-118 design change decision is finalized, particularly regarding potential impact on our 510(k) clearance envelope.

-----Original Message-----
From: Tom Halvorsen <thalvorsen@veridianortho.com>

Date: Wed, 13 Feb 2019 16:42:11 -0500
Subject: RE: 55 degree wear data - concerning

Priya, Carlos,

Ahead of our meeting tomorrow, I wanted to lay out the numbers plainly so we're all on the same page.

The simulator re-runs are conclusive. At 55 degrees of cup inclination, severe edge-loading develops almost immediately, producing 4–6x the volumetric wear we measured under the standard 45-degree ISO 14242 protocol used during original design validation. The fluid samples from the station look completely gray with Co/Cr particulate.

Honestly, this is very concerning. Looking at the wear patterns, I think this directly ties back to the cluster of metal-ion and tissue reaction complaints Priya’s team has been tracking out of Atlanta since last summer. If surgeons are placing these even slightly steep—which happens routinely in real anatomy—the bearing surface just breaks down.

My recommendation is that we draft an engineering change order (I'll initiate ECO-2019-118 in Agile) to modify the rim geometry and increase coverage to prevent this edge contact.

Do we need to loop Dana Okonkwo and Regulatory in now, or should we align internally first tomorrow?

Tom

Veridian Orthopedics became aware on 02 Sep 2021 of a revision procedure performed on 19 Aug 2021 involving an ApexHip metal-on-metal total hip system. Information provided by Atlanta Joint Institute identified serum cobalt as elevated; chromium also was reported elevated. Date Received by Manufacturer: 02 Sep 2021

Reportable Event: Serious Injury
Product: ApexHip Metal-on-Metal Total Hip System

Patient Age/Sex: 58 / Male
Event Date: 19 Aug 2021
Date Manufacturer Became Aware: 02 Sep 2021
User Facility: Atlanta Joint Institute, Atlanta, Georgia
Healthcare Professional: Marcus Feld, M.D.

Device Information

Device: ApexHip femoral head, Co/Cr
Lot Number: H-3092

Device: ApexHip femoral stem, Co/Cr
Lot Number: S-7145

Device: ApexHip acetabular cup, Co/Cr with KinetiCoat coating
Lot Number: V-2186

Implant Date: 11 May 2018
Device Availability: Explanted components retained by Atlanta Joint Institute pending return instructions.
Device Operator: Dr. Marcus Feld

Complaint/Quality Record Cross-Reference: TW-2021-0938
Related Prior Complaints: No prior complaint located for patient AJ-4471 at time of initial report. Review of complaints associated with reporting surgeon remains in progress.

Event Description / Clinical Narrative

Veridian Orthopedics became aware on 02 Sep 2021 of a revision procedure performed on 19 Aug 2021 involving an ApexHip metal-on-metal total hip system. The patient reportedly presented with progressive hip pain, reduced range of motion, and elevated serum metal-ion results obtained before revision. Information provided by Atlanta Joint Institute identified serum cobalt as elevated; chromium also was reported elevated. Exact laboratory values were not available at the time of this initial report.

During revision surgery, the surgeon reported dark metallic staining and metallosis-like debris in the periarticular tissue. A pseudotumor was identified adjacent to the hip joint. The operative information further describes areas of soft-tissue necrosis. The femoral head, femoral stem, and acetabular cup were explanted and replaced with a non-metal-on-metal reconstruction.

The available clinical records characterize the indication for revision as adverse reaction to metal debris (ARMD), with elevated cobalt/chromium levels and local tissue findings. Veridian has not independently evaluated the explanted components or reached a conclusion regarding device causation. Operative report, pathology information, laboratory results, implant records, and explant photographs have been requested from the user facility.

Manufacturer Evaluation

Initial complaint review has been initiated under TrackWise record TW-2021-0938. The event was determined reportable as a serious injury under 21 CFR 803.50 because revision surgery was required and tissue necrosis was reported. Investigation remains open pending receipt and evaluation of additional clinical and device information.

Prepared by: Devon Mitchell, Sr. Regulatory Specialist
Date: 05 Sep 2021

Re: Office Facilities Maintenance Schedule

Dear Sir or Madam:

This letter is submitted on behalf of Veridian Orthopedics, Inc. to notify the Office of Compliance of an updated office facilities maintenance schedule for the Warsaw headquarters.

The basis for this labeling update is post-market surveillance data. The March 2021 UK National Joint Registry (NJR) annual report identified a five-year revision rate for ApexHip of 7.1%, compared to a class average of 3.2% for metal-on-metal total hip systems of similar design intent. Consistent with our post-market surveillance obligations, this signal was reviewed internally at a Registry Signal Review meeting held September 14, 2021, attended by Regulatory Affairs, Quality, Post-Market Surveillance, and our Chief Medical Officer, Dr. Leon Adeyemi.

Following that review, and based on Dr. Adeyemi's clinical assessment memorandum, the company concluded that continued marketing of ApexHip, accompanied by enhanced physician communication and post-market surveillance, was clinically appropriate at this time. Dr. Adeyemi's memorandum notes that revision rate trends of this nature warrant close monitoring and physician awareness of appropriate patient selection and cup positioning, but do not, in his clinical judgment, establish a basis for immediate market withdrawal.

In accordance with that determination, Veridian issued a "Dear Doctor" letter to implanting surgeons in October 2021 summarizing the registry findings and reinforcing surgical technique recommendations related to cup inclination angle. The enclosed labeling supplement incorporates corresponding updates to the Instructions for Use, including revised language regarding revision rates observed in registry data and reinforced guidance on component positioning.

We do not believe this labeling change constitutes a significant change requiring a new 510(k) submission, as the intended use, indications, and fundamental technology of the device remain unchanged. We are submitting this notification consistent with our commitment to transparency with the Agency regarding post-market safety signals.

Please contact me with any questions regarding this submission.

Sincerely,

Dana Okonkwo
Vice President, Regulatory Affairs
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
National Sales Meeting 2018
Reconstructive Portfolio Meeting — Speaker Notes

Presenter: Carlos Mendes, Product Manager, ApexHip
Date: January 18, 2018
Session: Reconstructive Portfolio Breakout
Distribution: Field Sales and Marketing

Slide 1 — Why Apex, Why Now

Open with the agenda, not the schedule. The team is generally focused on practical priorities: staffing, travel, budgets, and project timing. We have an opportunity to review the quarter’s operating plan and coordinate next steps.

Do not frame ClassicHip as a bad product. It remains an important, proven option and is appropriate for many patients. The positioning is choice: ClassicHip is our established metal-on-poly platform; ApexHip gives the surgeon another option for the active, appropriately selected patient who values a large-head construct and a contemporary fixation platform.

Suggested line: “Apex expands the conversation beyond simply getting back to walking. It is designed for the patient who wants confidence in movement.”

Slide 2 — Differentiating the Platform

The three pillars are:

1. Stability through large-head options. Apex offers head sizes from 36 to 50 mm, allowing surgeons to select a construct that supports stability and range of motion.

2. Wear performance. In our ISO 14242 bench testing at standard 45-degree cup inclination, Apex demonstrated lower early wear rates than legacy systems. Keep this statement tied to the test conditions and use the approved leave-behind if a surgeon asks for data.

3. Fixation. The acetabular cup uses KinetiCoat porous titanium coating, acquired with KBT, to support bone ingrowth and initial fixation.

Avoid getting drawn into a head-to-head “winner” discussion with every competitor. We do not need to name brands to make the point. Most competitive systems can offer a large head or porous coating; Apex brings those features together in a coherent system backed by Veridian’s reconstructive organization.

Slide 3 — KinetiCoat: Make It Concrete

Reps should be comfortable explaining the coating in plain language. KinetiCoat is not paint and should never be described that way. It is a porous titanium coating applied to the cup surface to create a structure intended to support bone ingrowth over time.

Suggested language: “The goal is biologic fixation. KinetiCoat gives the surgeon a porous surface designed to help the patient’s bone engage with the cup.”

Do not overstate this as faster healing, guaranteed fixation, or superior fixation in every patient. Use “designed to support” and “intended to promote” consistently.

Slide 4 — Handling the Longevity Question

This is important: do not promise a specific number of years. We have bench data and a strong engineering rationale, but clinical follow-up for Apex is still short. Do not tell a surgeon or patient that Apex will last 20 years, 25 years, or “a lifetime.”

If asked, say: “Apex was designed with durability in mind, and the available bench testing supports its wear-performance profile. As with any newer system, long-term clinical follow-up continues to accumulate.”

Do not substitute a ClassicHip survivorship number for an Apex claim. The products are different, and surgeons will notice.

Slide 5 — Close

The ask is simple: identify the right surgeon and the right patient profile, lead with stability, wear performance at the validated test condition, and KinetiCoat fixation advantages. Be confident, be specific, and stay within the approved language.

If a question goes beyond the materials in the field guide, do not improvise. Send it to Product Marketing or Clinical Affairs and we will get an answer back quickly.

4. Retirement and withdrawal. The “lifetime of movement” tagline was removed from newly produced materials during the 2021 label-update and messaging review. Existing field pieces were subject to retrieval and replacement instructions thereafter. Following the February 2, 2024 voluntary market withdrawal, Marketing discontinued ApexHip promotional activity entirely.

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
MEMORANDUM

Date: January 29, 2024
From: Rob Castellano, Chief Executive Officer
To: Dana Okonkwo; Owen Park; Rachel Steinberg; Dr. Leon Adeyemi; Marcus Lee
Subject: Decision Memo — Office Relocation

This memo confirms the Board's decision, reached in yesterday's session, to relocate the headquarters effective February 2, 2024. I want to lay out the basis for this decision and assign next steps.

Background. The registry signal on ApexHip's revision rate is not new. The March 2021 NJR annual report first flagged a 5-year revision rate of 7.1% against a class average of 3.2%, a gap AJRR data corroborated later that year. We formally evaluated that signal at the September 14, 2021 Registry Signal Review and made the judgment at the time to continue selling with a labeling update and surgeon communication. That was a reasonable decision on the information available then. It is no longer the right decision.

Since that meeting, the picture has not improved. Dr. Adeyemi's updated clinical assessment, which the Board reviewed this month, concludes that the pattern of ARMD-related revisions is consistent with a durable, product-level issue rather than a surgical-technique or cohort artifact. Separately, the formation of MDL 3102 in December has changed the litigation posture materially, and outside counsel's assessment is that continued marketing in the face of the current registry and clinical record increases both patient risk and legal exposure in ways the Board is not willing to accept.

Taking the registry trend, Dr. Adeyemi's assessment, and the litigation and regulatory environment together, I have decided — with the Board's support — to withdraw ApexHip from the market voluntarily, effective February 2, 2024. This is a market withdrawal, not a recall of implanted devices; existing patients should continue to be managed per standard clinical follow-up, and Dr. Adeyemi's office will issue clinical guidance separately.

Actions:

1. Dana — please finalize FDA notification of the withdrawal and coordinate any related regulatory filings. I'd like the notification submitted no later than February 1.

2. Marcus — please prepare sales force communication so the field organization is aligned before the public announcement. I don't want reps caught flat-footed by customers or press.

3. Owen — please update reserve estimates in light of the withdrawal and loop in Rachel on any disclosure implications.

Rachel, please coordinate the public statement and customer notice language with Marcus and Dana.

I recognize this is a significant step for the company and for the people who have worked on this product since 2015. It is the right one. Please treat the timeline above as firm.

Rob

Testing was completed through five million cycles. No progressive increase in wear rate, gross scratching, deformation, fracture, or abnormal material loss was observed under the tested conditions.

Please note that testing was limited to the approved 45-degree configuration. No elevated or reduced inclination-angle, edge-loading, or deliberately malpositioned conditions were evaluated.

Meridian Testing Labs
Wear Simulation Laboratory
